about: Nokware's fixed text, in English, which is the source every other language is written from. 'critical' marks text someone may act on while in danger: it ships in another language only once a named person has reviewed that translation (see app/services/phrases.py). Everything here is written by hand and never translated while an answer is being written.

ask.no_information.text: I don't have information on that in the Ledger.
ask.no_information.note: The fixed reply the model is told to give; the API reads it back to set an answer's status, so it must match rag.NO_INFO_ANSWER in English.

ask.disagreement_lead.note: Opens a point where documents give different figures. The web looks for these words to show its note.

ask.safety_figures.text: Nokware doesn't publish figures on reports about someone's safety.
ask.safety_figures.note: Nokware's own counts are refused; AMA's published documents still answer.

ask.safety_in_documents.text: Here's what AMA's published documents say:

ask.no_safety_documents.text: The AMA documents Nokware searched don't report these figures either.

ask.document_chart_refusal.text: The tables in AMA's documents aren't yet read in a form that can be charted accurately, so I'd rather give you the figures in text than a chart that might be wrong.

ask.spreadsheet_refusal.text: I can't give you these figures as a spreadsheet: they're quoted from documents whose tables come out of the PDFs as loose numbers, so a sheet would invite sums the figures can't support. The figures are in the answer, and the documents themselves are linked below. Counts of residents' reports, and budget figures Nokware reads from AMA's budgets, do download as a spreadsheet.

ask.one_count.text: There's only one count here, so there's nothing to chart.

ask.one_month.text: There's only one month of reports so far, so there's nothing to chart over time.

ask.all_zero.text: Every count here is zero, so there's nothing to chart.

ask.machine_translated.text: Translated by machine from the English answer, which the sources are in.
ask.machine_translated.note: Shown with an answer written in another language, beside the way back to the English.

ask.translation_failed.text: This answer couldn't be translated reliably, so here it is in English.
ask.translation_failed.note: Used when the check finds a figure or a citation that doesn't match the English answer.

safety.steps.leave.text: If you can leave now, go to a neighbour, family, or the nearest police station.

safety.steps.dovvsu.text: At the police station, ask for DOVVSU, the domestic violence unit.
safety.steps.dovvsu.note: DOVVSU is the unit's own name and is never translated.

safety.steps.hurt.text: If you are hurt, go to a hospital or call 193.

safety.steps.someone_else.text: If it is someone else, a child or an adult, don't confront them yourself.
safety.steps.someone_else.note: A lost negative here tells someone to confront an abuser. This is why critical text waits for a reviewer.

safety.help_heading.text: In danger now? Call 112. If it fails, try the next number.

safety.call_list.text: Your call list may show you dialled Nokware: delete it if that is safer.

safety.numbers_offer.text: Send these numbers by SMS? Anyone with your phone could see them.

safety.medical.text: Nokware can't file this: it isn't an Assembly matter. Ambulance: 193, 0501 614 877, 0505 982 870. Or call 112.
safety.medical.note: The numbers are digits from the contacts data and are never translated; only the words around them are.

ask.no_figures_to_chart.text: There are no figures in this answer to chart.
ask.no_figures_to_chart.note: A chart was asked for, but the answer holds no figures at all — said instead of leaving the request unanswered.

ask.no_answer_to_chart.text: There's nothing to chart: the Ledger doesn't hold an answer to this yet.
ask.no_answer_to_chart.note: A chart was asked for on a question the Ledger can't answer.

ask.no_safety_chart.text: No chart either: these figures aren't published at all.
ask.no_safety_chart.note: A chart was asked for alongside figures about someone's safety, which Nokware never publishes.

ask.total_and_parts_only.text: The only figures here are a total and one part of it. A total drawn beside its parts reads as one of them, so there's nothing to chart.
ask.total_and_parts_only.note: Replaces the old, wrong 'only one count here' when a total was left out and one part remained.

speech.rest_on_screen.text: The rest of the answer is on the screen.
speech.rest_on_screen.note: Said at the end of a reading that had to stop short of the whole answer.

speech.sources_on_screen.text: The documents it comes from are listed with the answer.
speech.sources_on_screen.note: Closes every spoken answer: the sources are on the page, not in the audio.

speech.nothing_found.text: The page says where else to look, and how to request a document.
speech.nothing_found.note: Closes a spoken answer the Ledger couldn't answer.

speech.not_in_this_language.text: Reading aloud isn't available in this language yet.
speech.not_in_this_language.note: Shown where the Listen button would be. Nokware reads aloud only in languages whose fixed text it has written.

case.safety.received.note: A personal-safety case's status page and nothing else. Whoever holds the reference may not be the person who filed it, so the line says how far along the case is and never what it is about.

case.safety.in_progress.text: Your reference is being worked on.
case.safety.in_progress.note: The same neutral wording the SMS about a personal-safety case uses.

case.safety.closed.note: Says nothing about the outcome: an outcome would say what the case was.

petition.status.open.note: How a petition that is taking signatures is named, on every page and in the portal alike.

petition.status.awaiting_response.note: It reached its signatures; the MCE has 30 days to answer publicly.

petition.status.closed.note: Its 90 days ran out, or the person who started it closed it.

petition.status.removed.note: A contributor removed it on one of the four grounds. Only the ground, the date and the number remain.

petition.ground.private_individual.text: Names or attacks a private individual
petition.ground.private_individual.note: One of the four grounds, written the same way wherever it is read: the removal form, the tombstone, the report form, USSD and WhatsApp.

petition.ground.duplicate.note: The only ground that names another petition: its number is stored, so the tombstone can point there.

petition.ground.duplicate_comment.note: The same stored ground as petition.ground.duplicate, read about a comment: a comment repeats what is already on its own page and names no petition, so no number is asked for or stored.

petition.removal.duplicate_needs_code.text: Give the number of the open petition this one duplicates.

petition.removal.duplicate_not_found.text: No public petition has that number.

petition.removal.already_removed.text: This petition has already been removed.

petition.removal.own_petition.text: You started this petition, so you can't remove it. Another contributor can.
petition.removal.own_petition.note: A removal is a judgement on someone else's words; nobody judges their own.

petition.removal.signed_petition.text: You signed this petition, so you can't remove it. Another contributor can.

petition.removal.note_personal_data.text: This note holds personal data, such as a phone number, an email address or a Ghana Card number. Take it out: the note is kept in the Assembly's record.

petition.removal.note_too_long.text: Keep the note to 500 characters or fewer.

petition.report.note_too_long.text: Keep what you add to 300 characters or fewer.

petition.report.note_personal_data.text: What you added holds personal data, such as a phone number, an email address or a Ghana Card number. Take it out and say it another way.

petition.report.received.text: Thank you. A contributor will read this. The petition stays up while they do.
petition.report.received.note: Said to whoever reports a petition: a report never hides anything, and the wording must not suggest it did.

petition.report.already_removed.text: This petition has already been removed.

petition.dismissal.not_the_ground.note: One of the two fixed reasons a contributor dismisses a report with.

petition.edit.not_editable.text: This petition is closed, so it can't be edited.

petition.legacy.refused.text: Refused under the earlier review process
petition.legacy.refused.note: On a petition the MCE refused before Stage A. Never shown as a contributor's removal, which would be untrue.

petition.legacy.withdrawn.text: Withdrawn by the person who started it

petition.legacy.closed_in_move.text: Closed during the move to the new petition process

petition.comment.default_name.note: The name over a comment whose writer chose none. A comment never shows a number, so it shows this.

petition.comment.too_long.text: Keep your comment to 500 characters or fewer.

petition.comment.personal_data.text: Your comment holds personal data, such as a phone number, an email address or a Ghana Card number. Take it out and say it another way.
petition.comment.personal_data.note: Refused, never quietly mended: the person writing it decides how to say it instead.

petition.comment.private_individual.text: Your comment seems to name a private person. Comments on a petition are public, so say it without naming anyone.

petition.comment.removed.text: Comment removed by a verified contributor: {ground}
petition.comment.removed.note: What stands where a removed comment's words were. {ground} is one of the four grounds in the words a comment is judged by, which is petition.ground.duplicate_comment for a duplicate and petition.ground.* for the rest; a translation may put it wherever that language wants it.

petition.comment.already_removed.text: This comment has already been removed.

petition.comment.report_received.text: Thank you. A contributor will read this. The comment stays up while they do.
petition.comment.report_received.note: Said to whoever reports a comment: a report never hides anything, and the wording must not suggest it did.

petition.share.not_a_department.text: Choose a department from the Assembly's list.
petition.share.not_a_department.note: The list is the Assembly's own departments, in app/teams.py; there is no second list of them.

petition.share.already_shared.text: This petition has already been shared with that department.
petition.share.already_shared.note: Sharing it twice would ask for a second note from a department that writes one.

petition.note.not_shared.text: This petition wasn't shared with your department, so your department has no note to write on it.
petition.note.not_shared.note: Only the department the MCE shared a petition with answers on its page.

petition.note.already_written.text: Your department has already written its note on this petition. A note is published as it was written and stands as the department's answer.
petition.note.already_written.note: One note per department per petition, refused rather than replaced: an answer that can be rewritten is worth nothing to the person who was answered.

petition.note.too_long.text: Keep the note to 500 characters or fewer.

petition.note.personal_data.text: This note holds personal data, such as a phone number, an email address or a Ghana Card number. It is published on the petition's page, so take it out and say it another way.
petition.note.personal_data.note: Refused, never quietly mended: the officer writing it decides how to say it instead.

petition.note.private_individual.text: This note seems to name a private person. It is published on the petition's page, so say what the department is doing without naming anyone.

petition.reply.no_response.text: There is no response on this petition to reply to yet.
petition.reply.no_response.note: A reply answers the MCE's published response; until there is one, there is nothing to answer.

petition.reply.already_replied.text: You have already replied to this response. One reply stands under it.
petition.reply.already_replied.note: One response, one reply: a petition's page is a record of what was asked and what was answered, not a thread.

petition.reply.too_long.text: Keep your reply to 1,000 characters or fewer.

petition.reply.personal_data.text: Your reply holds personal data, such as a phone number, an email address or a Ghana Card number. Take it out and say it another way.
petition.reply.personal_data.note: The reply is published under the MCE's response, where anyone can read it.

petition.reply.private_individual.text: Your reply seems to name a private person. It is published under the MCE's response, so say it without naming anyone.

petition.sign.removed.text: This petition was removed, so it takes no more signatures.
petition.sign.removed.note: Refused the same way wherever a signature is offered. It says nothing of the petition, because the page behind that number is now the tombstone and says nothing of it either.

petition.channel.standing.note: How a petition's standing opens on a phone, on USSD and WhatsApp alike. {stage} is the status in the words petition.status.* gives it.

petition.channel.signatures_only.note: For a petition carrying no threshold, which is one written before a threshold was fixed at publication. It still says what it has.

petition.channel.removed.note: Built from the removal record alone, as the tombstone it repeats is. {ground} is one of the four grounds, in the words petition.ground.* gives it.

petition.channel.removed_nothing_public.text: Nothing of the petition is public.

petition.channel.removed_before_once.text: It had been removed once before.

petition.channel.removed_before.text: It had been removed {count} times before.

petition.channel.not_found_ussd.text: No petition has the number {number}. Check it and dial again.

petition.channel.not_found_whatsapp.text: No petition has the number {number}. Check it and send it again.
